High Myopia and Emmetropia: Exploratory Lens Expression Analysis

1 Overview

I compare expression in three high-myopia and three emmetropic human lens epithelial samples from NCBI GEO GSE136701. The aim is to explore sample relationships and test for differences between groups. This notebook reruns the existing R scripts; it does not rely on objects in the RStudio Global Environment. An internet connection is required for the GEO downloads.

This is an exploratory analysis of older adult surgical samples, not a clinical prediction tool. Probe-level results are not automatically gene-level findings.

2 Import the dataset

The import script downloads the GEO Series Matrix to a temporary file, then extracts expression values and metadata. Platform annotation is not downloaded.

3 Sample information and quality checks

Groups are assigned from recorded diagnoses, not assumed sample order. The quality-check script verifies alignment, checks finite values, and exports the sample table. The participants are aged 53–68 years. Emmetropia is the recorded control diagnosis, not a claim that all controls are otherwise healthy.

4 Expression-scale verification

GEO describes MAS 5.0 normalisation in GeneSpring 12.6.1 but does not explicitly identify the transformation scale in the inspected descriptions. The next script compares one submitted sample record against the matrix.

run_script("code/check_expression_scale.R")
##   Column             Description
## 1                       ID_REF =
## 2  VALUE MAS5.0 signal intensity
## 3                     ABS call =
## [1] "Raw data were normalized by MAS 5.0 algorithm, GeneSpring Software12.6.1 (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA, US)."
##               Probe Submitted    Matrix
## 1007_s_at 1007_s_at 11.870590 11.870590
## 1053_at     1053_at  9.219353  9.219353
## 117_at       117_at  5.868018  5.868018
## 121_at       121_at  9.495820  9.495820
## 1255_g_at 1255_g_at  5.888246  5.888246
## 1294_at     1294_at  7.235352  7.235352
## 
## Matched finite values: 54675 
## Non-positive submitted values: 63 
## Maximum difference without transformation: 0 
## Maximum difference after log2 transformation: 12.12801

For GSM4055612, all 54,675 submitted values matched the matrix exactly, with 63 non-positive values. This verifies import fidelity, not the original transformation. I retain the supplied values unchanged and report estimated effects as expression differences, not confirmed log2 fold changes. The appropriateness of this scale for linear modelling remains a limitation.

5 Exploratory analysis

# Requires the corrected version of this script: sample_clusters must be
# created before any axis command refers to its height.
run_script("code/03_exploratory_analysis.R")
## [1] 23.40 21.26

5.1 Expression distributions

The six samples have broadly similar medians and spreads. This does not establish that every sample is free from technical artefacts. Hiding outlier symbols in the boxplot does not remove observations from the analysis.

5.2 Principal component analysis

PCA uses all probes, with centring but no scaling to unit variance. PC1 explains 23.40% and PC2 explains 21.26% of variation. Together they account for 44.65%. The first two components do not show clear separation by diagnosis.

5.3 Sample clustering

Euclidean distance and complete linkage produce mixed diagnostic groups. No sample is excluded solely because of its position in this exploratory tree.

6 Differential expression analysis

The limma model compares High myopia minus Emmetropia, with diagnosis as its only predictor. Positive effects indicate higher expression in high myopia. Empirical Bayes moderation is followed by Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment across the probes. The selection rule is adjusted p-value below 0.05. Age and gender are not adjusted.

The model identifies 0 probes at adjusted p < 0.05. The smallest adjusted p-value is 0.2009. The observed zero-significant-probe result does not prove biological equivalence. The significant-probes CSV is expected to contain only headers when no probes pass the threshold.

7 Results visualisation

run_script("code/05_results_visualisation.R")

7.1 Expression differences and statistical evidence

The horizontal axis is the estimated expression difference. The vertical axis is negative log10 adjusted p-value. All points in the observed result fall below the 0.05 threshold line. Horizontal bands can occur when probes share adjusted p-values.

7.2 Exploratory top-30 heatmap

These probes were selected by the smallest unadjusted p-values in the same group comparison. Their apparent separation of diagnoses is therefore not independent validation. None passed the adjusted threshold in this analysis. Colours show row z-scores: red is above a probe’s own average and blue is below it. They do not compare absolute expression across different probes.

8 Discussion and conclusion

This workflow found no statistically significant probe-level differences at the specified adjusted threshold. The all-probe exploratory plots showed substantial within-group variation, while a selected-probe heatmap highlighted descriptive patterns. These findings have different purposes and are not contradictory.

Limitations include three samples per group, restriction to older adult lens surgical tissue, possible confounding, and incomplete documentation of the supplied expression scale. Raw-array quality checks, gene annotation, pathway analysis, and independent validation were not performed. Changing the name of the effect column does not resolve modelling assumptions. Larger independent samples and clarified preprocessing would be needed for stronger conclusions.

I reused publicly available study data and did not recruit participants or collect new tissue. The dataset-specific licence was not established during this project; public availability is not treated as proof of a particular licence.
